# Jeremiah 31 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** "At that time, declares the LORD, I will be the God of all the clans of Israel, and they shall be My people."

**2** Thus says the LORD: "The people who survived the sword found grace in the wilderness; when Israel sought for rest,

**3** The LORD appeared to him from far away. I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued My faithfulness to you.

**4** Again I will build you, and you shall be built, O virgin Israel! Again you shall adorn yourself with tambourines and shall go forth in the dance of the merrymakers.

**5** Again you shall plant vineyards on the mountains of Samaria; the planters shall plant and shall enjoy the fruit.

**6** For there shall be a day when watchmen will call in the hill country of Ephraim: 'Arise, and let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God.'"

**7** The LORD spoke concerning the restoration of Israel and the gathering from all the nations where He had scattered them.

**31** "Behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah,

**32** Not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, My covenant that they broke, though I was their husband, declares the LORD.

**33** For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I will put My law within them, and I will write it on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they shall be My people.

**34** And no longer shall each one teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, 'Know the LORD,' for they shall all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD. For I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more."

**35** The LORD declared the permanence of His covenant, as fixed as the ordinances of the sun, moon, and stars.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **31:3**: The 'everlasting love' (ahavat olam) is covenantal love — not sentiment but commitment. It grounds Israel's future in God's unchanging character.

- **31:31-34**: The New Covenant passage is the theological climax of the entire book. Quoted in full in Hebrews 8:8-12, it is the longest OT quotation in the NT. The covenant is 'new' not in replacing the Mosaic law but in internalizing it.

- **31:34**: 'Know the LORD' (yada YHWH) implies experiential, relational knowledge — not mere intellectual assent. The new covenant makes this universal among God's people.

— LOGOS
